BackstoryDef.title: Winter farmhand
BackstoryDef.description: Raised through short summers and brutal winters, this child learned to harvest every grain before the first frost reached the fields.

BackstoryDef.title: Holdfast smith's apprentice
BackstoryDef.description: A village smith taught them to mend axes, horseshoes, cooking pots, and whatever else a northern household could not afford to replace.

BackstoryDef.title: Stone hauler's child
BackstoryDef.description: They spent their youth hauling stone and timber for walls meant to survive northern winters and worse things beyond them.

BackstoryDef.title: Godswood carver
BackstoryDef.description: Quiet hours beneath ancient weirwoods were spent carving animals, faces, and the symbols of the old gods.

BackstoryDef.title: Ward of a Northern House
BackstoryDef.description: Sent to another northern lord's hall as a ward, they learned courtesy, history, household politics, and the importance of guest right.

BackstoryDef.title: Holdfast heir
BackstoryDef.description: As the expected successor to a small northern House, they were taught accounts, oaths, family history, and responsibility from childhood.

BackstoryDef.title: Spare son of the North
BackstoryDef.description: With no expectation of inheriting, the second son spent more time riding, hunting, and training in the yard.

BackstoryDef.title: Snow-born bastard
BackstoryDef.description: A bastard raised outside the lord's solar learned early that respect was earned rather than inherited.

BackstoryDef.title: Wolfswood hunter
BackstoryDef.description: They followed deer tracks through the Wolfswood and learned which animals would run, which would charge, and which should never be followed.

BackstoryDef.title: Winter Guard page
BackstoryDef.description: Serving northern men-at-arms meant carrying shields, cleaning weapons, and learning how to stop a wound from bleeding.

BackstoryDef.title: Frostfield farmer
BackstoryDef.description: Years of working thin northern soil taught them to make every harvest count and preserve food for long winters.

BackstoryDef.title: Castle forge smith
BackstoryDef.description: They forged tools, spearheads, nails, and armor for a northern holdfast where nothing useful was wasted.

BackstoryDef.title: Winter mason
BackstoryDef.description: They built thick stone walls, hearths, and roofs designed to carry the weight of heavy snow.

BackstoryDef.title: Wolfswood huntsman
BackstoryDef.description: A professional tracker of elk, boar, wolves, and outlaws, they know the northern forests better than most roads.

BackstoryDef.title: Hall carver
BackstoryDef.description: They decorated great halls with carved wolves, trees, heroic ancestors, and scenes from northern history.

BackstoryDef.title: Village bonesetter
BackstoryDef.description: Far from any maester, they learned to set bones, stitch wounds, and brew simple remedies from northern herbs.

BackstoryDef.title: Maester's assistant
BackstoryDef.description: Years spent grinding medicines and copying letters gave them more learning than most northern commoners.

BackstoryDef.title: Northern man-at-arms
BackstoryDef.description: They served their lord through border disputes, bandit attacks, and winters where guarding the food stores mattered as much as battle.

BackstoryDef.title: Holdfast steward
BackstoryDef.description: They managed stores, rents, servants, and disputes while their lord attended to matters of war and honor.

BackstoryDef.title: Guest-rights envoy
BackstoryDef.description: Trusted to speak between northern Houses, they understand old grudges, sworn oaths, and the sacred obligations of bread and salt.
